ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word has the same first sound as 'tie'? (1 mark)
   A. die
   B. fan
   C. van
   D. two

2. What does the abbreviation 'n.' mean in a dictionary entry? (1 mark)
   A. noun
   B. number
   C. name
   D. never

3. Which article goes before 'uniform'? (1 mark)
   A. one
   B. a
   C. an
   D. the

4. Which word has the same vowel sound as 'bird'? (1 mark)
   A. toy
   B. time
   C. turn
   D. card

5. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɔɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. bird
   B. car
   C. enjoy
   D. kite

6. Which question is indirect? (1 mark)
   A. Where did she cry?
   B. Why do you think the girl cried?
   C. Who cried?
   D. When did the girl cry?

7. A red octagon sign with the word STOP tells drivers to (1 mark)
   A. go faster
   B. turn on lights
   C. park
   D. stop completely

8. If you face the rising sun, north is on your (1 mark)
   A. left
   B. front
   C. right
   D. back

9. An adjective is a word that (1 mark)
   A. shows an action
   B. names a person
   C. joins sentences
   D. describes a noun

10. What is the superlative of 'good'? (1 mark)
   A. better
   B. best
   C. most good
   D. goodest

11. At the end of a statement, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. shouts
   B. rises
   C. hides
   D. falls

12. A high, rising voice when we say 'Really?' shows (1 mark)
   A. boredom
   B. anger only
   C. surprise
   D. sleep

13. Which quantifier goes with an uncountable noun in a question? (1 mark)
   A. much
   B. few
   C. many
   D. several

14. How do you make the question form of 'She is reading'? (1 mark)
   A. She is reading?
   B. Is she reading?
   C. Does she reading?
   D. Is reading she?

15. What is an inference? (1 mark)
   A. A word from the text copied exactly
   B. Something not stated directly that you work out from clues
   C. The title of a passage
   D. A spelling mistake

16. What is the contraction of 'I am'? (1 mark)
   A. Im'
   B. I'm
   C. Ia'm
   D. I'am

17. Which of these is NOT an adverb? (1 mark)
   A. tidy
   B. nearby
   C. slowly
   D. early

18. What does 'rinse' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To dry with cloth
   B. To make dirty
   C. To wash with clean water to take off soap
   D. To cook

19. What does 'rinse' mean in the passage on hand washing? (1 mark)
   A. To wash off soap with clean water
   B. To add soap
   C. To dry the hands
   D. To hide germs

20. Why do flies spread germs? (1 mark)
   A. They sleep on beds
   B. They eat all the soap
   C. They land on waste and then on food
   D. They drink clean water

21. How long is a descriptive composition at this level? (1 mark)
   A. 200 to 300 words
   B. 10 to 20 words
   C. 500 words
   D. 80 to 100 words

22. What should you do to listen fluently to a speech? (1 mark)
   A. Draw during the speech
   B. Face the speaker and listen for the main points
   C. Look at your phone
   D. Talk to a friend

23. In netball, what must a player do with the ball after catching it? (1 mark)
   A. Run with it
   B. Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   C. Sit on it
   D. Kick it

24. Which question word asks about ownership? (1 mark)
   A. where
   B. when
   C. whose
   D. who

25. Which question is correct for asking about the owner of some boots? (1 mark)
   A. Whose boots are these?
   B. Who boots are these?
   C. Whose are boot these?
   D. Whose is these boots?

26. Which tense do we usually use for earlier events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. Command
   B. Question form
   C. Past tense
   D. Future tense

27. Which word has a silent w? (1 mark)
   A. write
   B. water
   C. window
   D. week

28. What is tax? (1 mark)
   A. A bank loan
   B. Money given as a prize
   C. A kind of market
   D. Money that people pay to the government

29. Why is it good to read a newspaper regularly? (1 mark)
   A. It replaces school
   B. You learn what is happening and new words
   C. It gives you money
   D. It cannot teach anything

30. Which preposition shows movement from one side to the other inside something, such as a gate? (1 mark)
   A. through
   B. under
   C. near
   D. over

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Punctuate: 'we planted maize beans and sorghum' (2 marks)

32. Write the past participle of: write, see, take. (3 marks)

33. Correct the spellings: peple, libary, beutiful. (3 marks)

34. List three parts of a diary entry. (3 marks)

35. Write two words with the sound /uː/ and two words with /ʊ/. (2 marks)

36. Describe how to make the sounds /f/ and /v/ and say how they are different. Give one example pair. (4 marks)

37. Write four sentences about cleaning your classroom that use and, but, so and or. (4 marks)

38. Explain the difference between 'who' and 'whose'. Give one question for each. (3 marks)

39. Write four sentences using words with double consonants that you have learnt. (4 marks)

40. Explain the difference between 'but' and 'so' with an example of each. (4 marks)

41. Name the five senses and say why a descriptive writer uses them. (3 marks)

42. Write three ways to make your speech clearer. (3 marks)

43. Explain the difference between 'it's' and 'its' with one sentence for each. (4 marks)

44. Write the subject and the object forms of: I, he, we, they. (2 marks)

45. Copy in neat print: 'Please listen carefully.' Circle the silent letter. (2 marks)

46. Write a question for each answer: (a) 'It is at the stadium.' (b) 'The coach.' (2 marks)

47. Give two things you can add to a pictorial composition that are not in the pictures. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — two
   Tie and two both begin with /t/. Die starts with /d/.

2. A — noun
   The letter n. shows that the word is a noun.

3. B — a
   Uniform starts with the consonant sound 'yoo'.

4. C — turn
   Bird and turn both have /ɜː/.

5. C — enjoy
   Enjoy has the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

6. B — Why do you think the girl cried?
   The answer must be worked out from clues.

7. D — stop completely
   A stop sign means stop.

8. A — left
   The sun rises in the east. When you face east, north is on your left.

9. D — describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

10. B — best
   Good, better, best.

11. D — falls
   Statements usually end with a fall.

12. C — surprise
   A rising voice can show surprise.

13. A — much
   How much water?

14. B — Is she reading?
   Put is before the subject.

15. B — Something not stated directly that you work out from clues
   Inferential questions need you to use clues.

16. B — I'm
   The apostrophe replaces the a in am.

17. A — tidy
   'Tidy' is an adjective.

18. C — To wash with clean water to take off soap
   You rinse after using soap.

19. A — To wash off soap with clean water
   You rinse after soap.

20. C — They land on waste and then on food
   Flies carry germs from waste to food.

21. D — 80 to 100 words
   The task calls for 80 to 100 words.

22. B — Face the speaker and listen for the main points
   Active listening means paying attention to the main points.

23. B — Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   The passage says players cannot run with the ball.

24. C — whose
   'Whose' asks who owns something.

25. A — Whose boots are these?
   'Whose' is followed by a noun.

26. C — Past tense
   Events that already happened use the past tense.

27. A — write
   In 'write' the w is silent.

28. D — Money that people pay to the government
   Tax pays for services such as roads and schools.

29. B — You learn what is happening and new words
   Regular reading builds knowledge and vocabulary.

30. A — through
   'Through' shows movement within.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: We planted maize, beans and sorghum.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each comma and capital/full stop.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: written, seen, taken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: people, library, beautiful
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Day and date; greeting (Dear Diary); body (events and feelings); sign-off. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: /uː/: food, spoon. /ʊ/: book, cook.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Touch the top teeth to the lower lip and blow. /f/ is whispered and /v/ is voiced with a buzz. Example: fan and van.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mouth position, 1 mark for /f/ whispered, 1 mark for /v/ voiced, 1 mark for the pair.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences, each with the named conjunction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Who' asks about a person: Who is the coach? 'Whose' asks about the owner: Whose ball is this?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences with correctly spelt double consonant words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'But' shows a difference: It was late, but we stayed. 'So' shows a result: It was late, so we left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sight, sound, smell, touch and taste. They help the reader to imagine the thing being described.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the senses and 1 for the reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open your mouth enough; speak slowly at first; listen to a good model and copy them; practise every day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: It's means 'it is' or 'it has': It's raining. Its shows belonging: The dog wagged its tail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: I, me; he, him; we, us; they, them.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each pair.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Please listen carefully. (silent t in listen)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat copying and 1 mark for identifying t.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) Where is it? (b) Who is the man with the whistle?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: What people say, and how people feel or think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
